extName.description: Extension name — the Chrome Web Store title AND the label in the toolbar / chrome://extensions. For each locale, localize with that language's 'reader mode' search term for ASO, keeping the 'Open Book' brand (e.g. de: 'Open Book — Lesemodus', es: 'Open Book — Modo Lectura').

extSummary.message: Distraction-free reader mode: read articles as a two-page book you flip with arrows. Plus an image gallery. Private, open source.
extSummary.description: Store short description / summary shown under the title. HARD max 132 characters — verify each locale's translation stays under the limit.

welcomeTagline.message: Open Book Reader turns any article into a calm, two-page reading view.

welcomeStep1Title.message: Pin it so it's one click away

welcomeStep1Body.message: New extensions hide in Chrome's toolbar menu. Pin Open Book Reader so you can always reach it.

welcomeStep1Pin.message: Click 🧩 in the toolbar, then 📌 pin Open Book Reader

welcomeStep2Body.message: Go to a news story, blog post, or long page you'd like to read without the clutter.

welcomeStep3Body.message: Click the 📖 toolbar icon, or press Alt+B for text (Alt+Shift+B for images). Use the arrow keys to turn pages, and Esc to close.

welcomeCta.message: Try it on a sample article →

welcomeCtaHint.message: Opens a clean article in a new tab — activate the reader there to see it in action.

welcomePrivacy.message: 🔒 Everything happens on your device. Open Book Reader collects nothing and sends nothing to the developer.

permWhyDefault.message: This feature needs an additional permission.

permWhyZip.message: To bundle a ZIP, Open Book Reader needs permission to fetch the selected images from the sites they live on. The files are saved only to your device — nothing is sent anywhere else.

permWhyDownloads.message: Open Book Reader needs permission to save files to your Downloads folder.

permWhyAutoOpen.message: To open reading mode automatically on $HOST$, Open Book Reader needs permission to check that site’s pages when they load. Everything stays on your device — nothing is collected or sent anywhere.

optGuideOpenTitle.message: Open it on any page — three ways:

optGuideOpenToolbar.message: Toolbar icon — smart pick: the 📖 reader for articles, the 🖼 gallery for image-heavy pages.

optGuideOpenRightClick.message: Right-click a page or image → Open in Book Reader → Auto / Reader / Gallery.

optGuideOpenWhy.message: Want a site to always open one way? Right-click → Always open this site as Reader / Gallery, or add a path/wildcard pattern under Per-site rules below. Want zero clicks? Right-click → Auto-open on this site — content pages there open by themselves, list pages never do, and Esc always closes.

optGuideReadFlip.message: <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> flip pages — or click the left / right edge of the book

optGuideReadTopbar.message: Topbar: ⊞ columns (2/3/4) · theme · <kbd>A−</kbd> / <kbd>A+</kbd> font size · 🖼 switch to gallery

optGuideWrongTitle.message: Picked the wrong content? Sometimes the reader grabs a sidebar or the wrong block. Three ways to fix it:

optGuideWrongSelect.message: Select the text on the page first, then open the reader — it reads just your selection.

optGuideWrongPick.message: Click ⌖ Pick in the topbar, then click the block you want — the reader re-reads from there.

optGuideWrongSave.message: After picking, Save for this site so it's reused automatically next time. Saved picks live under Saved content picks below, where you can fine-tune the CSS selector or remove them.

optGuideGalleryLayout.message: Wall / Ordered layout toggle — Ordered reads images in order, row by row; Size at max = one page at a time (webtoons, manga)

optGuideGalleryLightbox.message: Click a tile for the lightbox — <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> browse · <kbd>Esc</kbd> close

optGuideGalleryFit.message: ⟷ Fit width in the lightbox reads a tall page by scrolling — F toggle

optGuideGalleryLoadAll.message: ⟳ Load all pulls lazy images · select tiles to download or ZIP · 📖 switch to reader

optGuideGalleryHide.message: ⊘ Hide on a tile filters avatars & repeated noise (per site) — hover a scope to preview what disappears

optGuideShortcutsWhy.message: Chrome controls these — they can't be edited inside the extension. Open Chrome's shortcut editor to set your own.

optPageTurnHint.message: How pages flip: a 3D book page, a soft paper curl, a simple slide, or instant. Respects your “reduce motion” setting.

optMaxWidthHint.message: Default Full (fills the window). Drag left to cap line width for easier reading.

optReadSelHint.message: If you've selected text on the page when you open the reader, read just that selection instead of the whole page - a quick override for when auto-extraction grabs the wrong content. Off = always read the whole page.

optPrintUrlHint.message: When you 🖨 Print / Save as PDF, add a footer with the page's full URL so the saved copy links back to the article. Off = omit it.

optPicksHint.message: When the reader grabs the wrong block, the ⌖ Pick button lets you choose the real content and Save for this site. Saved picks are listed here and reused automatically on that site. You can edit the CSS selector to fine-tune it: a class like .article-body is more robust than the auto-generated path, and a selector that matches several blocks (e.g. .intro, .post-body) reads them all. The ✓/✗ marks whether the selector is valid. Remove one to go back to automatic extraction.

optGalColumnsHint.message: How many columns the Wall (masonry) layout uses — fewer = larger images. Clamped per screen, so the in-gallery Size slider always tops out at a 2-column view.

optGalOrderedColsHint.message: Default columns for the Ordered (in-order) layout, where images read row by row. 1 = one page at a time (a centered reading strip). Each site remembers its own layout + size.

optGalFitWidthHint.message: In the big-image view, fit a tall page to the width and scroll down it (for reading manga / comic / scan pages) instead of shrinking the whole page to fit. Toggle live with the lightbox ⟷ button or the F key.

optGalHideAvatarsHint.message: Auto-filter avatars, emoji and badges out of the gallery (the profile-pic clutter on forums & comment threads) — detected by their profile links and avatar/gravatar/emoji markup, not by size, so album art and product shots stay. Hide anything it misses with the ⊘ Hide button on a tile.

optHiddenHint.message: The per-site image filter. The ⊘ Hide button in the gallery drops an image (or its folder / host) from the wall — useful for avatars, badges and other repeated noise. Hidden patterns are listed here as URL globs (* = wildcard). Entries starting with css: match images by their place in the page instead of by URL. Remove one to bring those images back.

optGalAutoLoadHint.message: Progressively pull the page's lazy images as you near the end of the grid (prefetched so tiles are ready). Off = only show what's already loaded, plus the manual ⟳ Load all button.

optGalScrollSpeedHint.message: Hands-free auto-scroll speed (toolbar Auto-scroll button / A key; +/- to nudge), in pixels per second. Lower = slower browsing.

optGalSlideSpeedHint.message: Seconds each image is shown when you play the slideshow in the big-image view (lightbox ▶ button / A key; +/- to nudge). Plays once and stops on the last image.

optSecSmartSub.message: when you click the toolbar icon

optAutoGalleryHint.message: Toolbar-icon click opens 🖼 gallery instead of 📖 reader when the page has at least this many images. Off = always open the reader. (Alt+B / Alt+Shift+B always honor their mode.)

optKeepReaderHint.message: When auto-opening by image count, stay in the 📖 reader if the page has at least this many words of article text - so a long illustrated read isn't sent to the gallery. Off = decide by image count only.

optRulesHint.message: Force a mode on specific sites instead of the smart auto-pick. The pattern matches host + path with * as a wildcard — example.com (whole site), example.com/blog/* (a section), *.example.com/* (all subdomains). When several match, the most specific wins. Applies to the toolbar icon and right-click menu; Alt+B / Alt+Shift+B always honor their own mode. Auto-open goes one step further: matching pages that look like real content (an article body, an image set) open in reading mode with no click at all — list and search pages stay untouched, and Esc always closes. It asks once for permission to run on that site.

optRuleActAutoSmart.message: opens by itself when the page looks like an article or gallery

optRuleActManualSmart.message: sets the default mode; opens on click

optRuleActManualMode.message: sets the default mode to $MODE$; opens on click

optAutoHint.message: Open reading mode automatically on matching content pages (asks once for a site permission). List and search pages stay untouched.

optAutoNoPattern.message: This pattern can’t auto-open — its host part can’t form a site permission (remove the mid-host wildcard).

optNoteSync.message: Settings sync across devices signed into the same browser profile.

optNotePrivacy.message: Privacy: collects no data and sends nothing to the developer. It runs on a page only when you invoke it (toolbar icon, shortcut, or right-click menu) — or on sites where you explicitly turned auto-open on. It makes network requests only when you explicitly download images from the gallery.

optNoteOpenSource.message: Open source: this extension is fully open — read every line, verify the privacy claims, file an issue, or contribute at github.com/kouxing2000/open-book-reader.

optNoPickForSite.message: No saved pick for $SITE$ yet. Use the ⌖ Pick button on that site.

optNoPicks.message: No saved picks yet. Use the ⌖ Pick button in the reader, then “Save for this site”.

optRevertTitle.message: Revert to the selector from when this page opened
